clue.text: Low bash organised by lad with nothing lacking

indicators.note: organised tells us the letters of bash are put into a new order
lacking tells us the zero is dropped from the word for the lad

parts.note: a lad is a boy
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A dismal party is thrown together by a young man who has everything he needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges BASH into SHAB; 'lacking' takes O out of BOY to leave BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby behaviour is mean and contemptible, the same sense as a low trick.

clue.text: Squeeze into space pump, say, with instrument

parts.note: a pump is one kind of shoe, hence 'say'
a horn is a brass musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone squeezes a pump into a tight spot with the help of some tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoehorn something is to force it into a space too small for it, an idiom from the shoe-fitting tool.

clue.text: Modify piece of local terminology

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to change a bit of regional jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify something is to change it a little, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Went on water around lake in a puffed-up state?

indicators.note: around tells us the boating word wraps round the letter for lake

parts.note: to boat is to travel on water, so went on water is boated
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone rowed round a lake and came back swollen with pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloated means swollen or inflated, the same as puffed up.

clue.text: Preliminary entertainment with a jolly at college

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
to be up is to be in residence at university, a British usage

explanation.surface: A student's warm-up act involves a fun outing at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is not merry here: it is navy slang for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm-up is an act staged before the main show to get an audience going.

clue.text: Estate maybe with line by the sound of it providing support for TV presenters

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, or auto, hence 'maybe'

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: a line of people waiting is a queue

explanation.surface: A station wagon parked beside a queue somehow helps people who read the news.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is a British car with a long rear load area, a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocue is the screen device that scrolls a script for presenters to read on camera.

clue.text: Clear root of orthodoxy in a set of party goals

parts.note: manifest means plain or clear

indicators.note: root of picks the opening letter, the start from which a word grows

explanation.surface: A political document plainly grounded in traditional belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is the published programme of aims a political party stands on.

clue.text: Cushion not well held by prisoner

indicators.note: held by puts the word for unwell inside the prisoner abbreviation

parts.note: POW stands for prisoner of war
not well means ill

explanation.surface: A sick inmate is given something soft to rest on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is a soft cushion for the head.

clue.text: Flattery from gentle older citizen defending son

parts.note: gentle means soft
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
OAP is old-age pensioner, British for a retired person

explanation.surface: A mild pensioner sticks up for their boy with sweet talk.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP, old-age pensioner, is everyday British for an elderly retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is persuasive flattery, an idiom for smooth talk.

clue.text: Short price I misread is out of date

indicators.note: misread suggests the letters were taken in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone misreads a cut-price label and finds it expired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short price' looks like a bargain, but all three words SHORT PRICE I are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric is used humorously for something hopelessly old-fashioned or dated.

clue.text: Conflict beginning to tarnish point of view

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an angle is a perspective or point of view

explanation.surface: A dispute starts to sully someone's outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle can mean a fight or quarrel, as in to tangle with someone.

clue.text: One revered actor on radio

indicators.note: on radio means the word is heard rather than seen, so its sound counts

parts.note: John Thaw was a British actor, famous as TV detective Inspector Morse

explanation.surface: A well-loved performer is heard on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent THAW and the Norse god's name are said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse thunder god was worshipped, so he is a being once revered.

clue.text: Companion with idiot largely stuck in river getting condition from dampness?

indicators.note: stuck in places the companion and idiot pieces inside the river name

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a fool is an idiot

explanation.surface: A friend and a fool get stuck in a river and suffer from the wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the idiot word's last letter; the Trent flows through the English Midlands. 'stuck in' governs both the companion and the shortened idiot together.
explanation.definitionFit: Trench foot is a foot disease caused by long exposure to cold and wet, notorious in First World War trenches.

clue.text: Inner self is transformed to include depth and social quality?

indicators.note: to include puts the abbreviation for depth inside the rearranged letters
transformed tells us these letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone's inner being changes to gain profundity and charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges INNER SELF IS; 'to include' slips D among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sociable and warm towards others is a quality of character.

clue.text: Impression made by English students' event with French wine included

indicators.note: included puts the French wine inside the student event

parts.note: rag is a British student charity festival
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A British university festival with French wine leaves its mark.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG week is a British student fund-raising event.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is a print taken from an engraved plate, an impression.

clue.text: Area supporting leading Lib Dem in a familiar way?

parts.note: pro means in favour of

parts.words: leading Lib Dem in a familiar way
parts.note: Vince Cable, former Liberal Democrat leader, by his first name

explanation.surface: A region backs a top Liberal Democrat with casual friendliness.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a British party; Vince Cable led them 2017-19.
explanation.definitionFit: A province is a region or administrative area of a country.

clue.text: Act in accordance with directors and be ignored

parts.note: to go by a rule is to follow it
a company's directors form the board

explanation.surface: Obeying the management may just mean being overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by the board is an idiom for being abandoned or disregarded.

clue.text: Robert with snow now disappearing was first in winter vehicle

parts.note: Bob is a familiar form of Robert

indicators.note: disappearing says the given letters vanish from the word before them

parts.note: the word now is removed as written
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: Robert was in the lead in a sledge as the snow melted away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now disappearing' strips NOW from SNOW, leaving S.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobsled is a racing sledge used on ice tracks in winter.

clue.text: Delightful place is by yard with cross outside, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means the assembled letters are seen as in a mirror, backwards
outside puts the hybrid animal round the other letters

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and donkey
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lovely spot reveals itself beside a yard with a hybrid animal standing guard.
explanation.walkthrough: MULE round ISY gives MUISYLE, which 'on reflection' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Elysium was the paradise of the blessed, so any blissful place.

clue.text: Look up in support of good man and actress

indicators.note: in a down clue, being in support of means sitting below

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Gazing upwards while backing a saint and an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is a celebrated American film actress.

clue.text: Street by harsh Northern town reportedly offering fruit

parts.note: raw weather is harsh

indicators.note: reportedly says to hear the town name as a word pronounced alike

parts.note: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, northern England

explanation.surface: A road next to a bleak northern town reportedly sells fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury, in north-west England, is pronounced like 'berry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strawberry is a red soft fruit.

clue.text: What footballers might do illegitimately in dodgy club

definitions.meaning: players fake a fall to win a free kick or penalty
a seedy, disreputable bar or nightclub

explanation.definitionFit: Dive means both a faked fall in football and a sleazy drinking den.

clue.text: Peculiar media boss on the way up? Object

indicators.note: on the way up in a down clue means writing the letters bottom to top

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
ED, editor, runs a newspaper

explanation.surface: An odd newspaper chief climbing the ladder raises a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection, so a verb synonym of object.

clue.text: Lowly chaps with bottle getting very shortly excluded

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: excluded says the abbreviated letter is left out of the bottle word

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle
V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: Humble men with a bottle are soon shut out.
explanation.definitionFit: Menial work is low-status and servile.

clue.text: Thick piece around lunchtime for squirrel

indicators.note: around puts the chunk round the time

parts.note: a chunk is a thick piece
lunchtime is 1 p.m., written IPM with I as one

explanation.surface: A thick slab of food eaten around midday ends up with a squirrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime is 1PM, with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipmunk is a small striped ground squirrel.

clue.text: Old man taking in a deity in temple

indicators.note: taking in puts the god inside the father word

parts.note: an old man is a father, pa
a deity is a god

explanation.surface: A father welcomes a god into a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Buddhist or Hindu temple tower in Asia.

clue.text: Issue in which say a body of engineers needs backing

indicators.note: backing says these pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A question on which an engineering corps needs support.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come out, the same as to emerge.
